title: Contributing to phiper
text: Fork package clone onto computer. haven’t done , recommend using usethis::create_from_github("Polymerase3/phiper", fork = TRUE). Install development dependencies devtools::install_dev_deps(), make sure package passes R CMD check running devtools::check(). R CMD check doesn’t pass cleanly, ’s good idea ask help continuing. Create Git branch pull request (PR). recommend using usethis::pr_init("brief-description--change"). Make changes, commit git, create PR running usethis::pr_push(), following prompts browser. title PR briefly describe change. body PR contain Fixes #issue-number. user-facing changes, add bullet top NEWS.md (.e. just first header). title: Alpha Diversity Analysis in PhIP-seq
text: Alpha diversity quantifies within-sample variety reactive peptides. PhIP-seq, sample’s enrichment profile can characterised many unique peptide species enriched (richness), evenly enrichment distributed (evenness), dominated single peptide (dominance). properties change across disease conditions, timepoints, patient subgroups, making alpha diversity useful summary statistic exploratory analysis hypothesis testing. vignette walks complete alpha diversity workflow phiper: Computing diversity metrics compute_alpha() Visualising distributions plot_alpha() plot_alpha_interactive() Testing group differences compute_alpha_significance() Summarising statistical results plot_alpha_significance()

title: Alpha Diversity Analysis in PhIP-seq
text: Threshold mode re-defines “present” using continuous abundance column (fold_change default). peptides whose fold-change exceeds threshold counted. Raising threshold sharpens definition “hit” typically reduces richness. Supply abundance_col use different column fold_change:

text: compute_distance() builds sample × feature abundance matrix phip_data object computes pairwise distances samples. normalised abundance matrix attached returned dist object "abundances" attribute — reused downstream compute_pcoa_feature_associations() compute_capscale().

text: compute_pcoa() wraps stats::cmdscale() returns S3 object class "beta_pcoa" containing sample coordinates, eigenvalues, variance explained, eigenvalue diagnostics. eigen_diagnostics tibble reports many eigenvalues negative large relative positive ones. Non-Euclidean distances (Bray-Curtis) routinely produce small fraction negative eigenvalues; ratio ~0.1 generally acceptable. negative eigenvalues substantial, apply Lingoes Cailliez correction:

title: Beta Diversity Analysis in PhIP-seq
text: PERMANOVA (permutational ANOVA) tests whether group centroids differ significantly multivariate distance space. compute_permanova() runs global model pairwise post-hoc contrasts, optional BH adjustment within contrast scope. scope column distinguishes three levels inference: p_adjust applied within scope separately, global pairwise p-values adjusted independently. Repeated measures. subject_col provided subjects appear multiple timepoints, permutations time contrasts stratified subject. simplified approximation; complex longitudinal designs may require custom permutation schemes via permute::().
code: perm_res <- compute_permanova(   dist_obj     = d,   ps           = pd,   group_col    = "group",   time_col     = "timepoint",   subject_col  = "subject_id",   permutations = 99L,   p_adjust     = "BH" ) #> [19:44:16] INFO  preparing distance labels and metadata. #> [19:44:16] INFO  building metadata from `ps`. #> [19:44:16] INFO  filtering samples with missing grouping variables. #> [19:44:16] INFO  subsetting distance matrix to complete cases. #> [19:44:16] INFO  preparing global permanova model. #> [19:44:16] INFO  running global permanova #>                    - model: d_resp ~ group + timepoint + group * timepoint #>                    - permutations stratified by subject #> [19:44:16] INFO  running pairwise permanova contrasts.  perm_res #> # A tibble: 5 × 8 #>   scope          contrast term            F_stat      R2 p_value p_adjust n_perm #>   <chr>          <chr>    <chr>            <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>  <int> #> 1 global         <global> group          252.    0.764      0.01     0.03     99 #> 2 global         <global> timepoint        0.995 0.00302    0.42     0.44     99 #> 3 global         <global> group:timepoi…   0.990 0.00300    0.44     0.44     99 #> 4 group_pairwise A vs B   group          252.    0.763      0.01     0.01     99 #> 5 time_pairwise  T1 vs T2 timepoint        0.995 0.00302    0.35     0.35     99

title: Delta Analysis in PhIP-seq
text: aggregate_stat controls peptide-level z-scores combined: "stouffer" (default) — weighted Stouffer combination "maxmean" — mean dominant direction "af" — absolute fraction strat_bins bins peptides pooled prevalence aggregation. default bins c(0.002, 0.005, ..., 0.50) stratify across prevalence range low- high-prevalence peptides treated separately. Set strat_bins = 0 single global statistic without stratification.
code: # No stratification delta_nostrat <- compute_delta(   pd,   rank_cols      = "peptide_id",   group_cols     = "group",   strat_bins     = 0,   B_permutations = 2000L )  # Custom bins delta_custom <- compute_delta(   pd,   rank_cols      = "peptide_id",   group_cols     = "group",   strat_bins     = c(0.05, 0.25, 0.50),   B_permutations = 2000L )

title: phiper - Automated PhIP-seq Analysis and Reporting
text: phiper organised four analysis domains, dedicated computation visualisation functions: Enrichment counts — plot_enrichment_counts() gives quick overview per-group peptide hit counts. Alpha diversity — richness, Shannon, Simpson, Pielou evenness, Berger-Parker dominance, optional significance testing bracket annotations (compute_alpha(), compute_alpha_significance()). Beta diversity — pairwise distances, PCoA, CAP (constrained ordination), PERMANOVA, dispersion tests, t-SNE (compute_distance(), compute_pcoa(), compute_capscale(), compute_permanova(), compute_dispersion(), compute_tsne()). Global prevalence shift (delta) — subject-level permutation tests antigen-wide prevalence shifts groups, forest plots ECDF visualisations (compute_delta(), forestplot(), ecdf_plot()). Per-feature prevalence comparison (POP) — Fisher’s exact McNemar tests every peptide taxonomic rank, visualised scatter plots volcano plots (compute_pop(), scatter_static(), volcano_static()).

title: Global Shift in Peptide-level Prevalence via Subject-level Permutation — compute_delta
text: stratum (rank, feature, group_col) defines ordered pair groups (g1, g2), procedure : Peptide-level prevalences. peptide, prevalences g1 g2 $$      \hat p_k = \frac{x_k}{n_k},\quad k \\{g1, g2\},    $$ x_k number samples presence (exist > 0) n_k number distinct samples (paired subjects). Per-peptide effect z-score (stat_mode). "diff": effect \(\Delta = \hat p_{g2} - \hat p_{g1}\) $$        SE = \sqrt{\hat p_{g1}(1 - \hat p_{g1}) / n_{g1} +                   \hat p_{g2}(1 - \hat p_{g2}) / n_{g2}} ,      $$ z-score \(z = \Delta / SE\) (small floor SE). "asin": variance-stabilized difference angles, $$        z = \frac{\arcsin \sqrt{\hat p_{g2}} - \arcsin \sqrt{\hat p_{g1}}}                 {\sqrt{1 / (4 n_{g1}) + 1 / (4 n_{g2})}} .      $$ "score": pooled score z equality proportions (2×2 score test), using raw proportions \(\tilde p_k = x_k / n_k\) pooled \(\tilde p = (x_1 + x_2)/(n_1 + n_2)\): $$        z = \frac{\tilde p_{g2} - \tilde p_{g1}}                 {\sqrt{\tilde p(1-\tilde p)\left(1/n_{g1} + 1/n_{g2}\right)}} .      $$ "srlr": signed root likelihood ratio \(H_0: p_{g1}=p_{g2}\): $$        LR = 2\left[\ell(\hat p_{g1};x_1,n_1)+\ell(\hat p_{g2};x_2,n_2)                  -\ell(\hat p;x_1,n_1)-\ell(\hat p;x_2,n_2)\right],      $$ $$        z = \mathrm{sign}(\hat p_{g2}-\hat p_{g1})\sqrt{LR},      $$ \(\ell(p;x,n)=x\log p+(n-x)\log(1-p)\) \(\hat p_{gk}=x_k/n_k\), \(\hat p=(x_1+x_2)/(n_1+n_2)\). "mcnemar" (paired-): signed McNemar z based discordant pairs \(b = \#(g1=1,g2=0)\), \(c = \#(g1=0,g2=1)\): $$        z = \frac{b - c}{\sqrt{b + c}} .      $$ \(b+c=0\), z defined 0. "srlr_paired" (paired-): signed root deviance paired binomial problem \(m=b+c\): $$        z = \mathrm{sign}(b-c)\sqrt{2\left[b\log\frac{2b}{m} + c\log\frac{2c}{m}\right]} .      $$ Terms \(0\log 0\) defined 0; \(m=0\), z 0. \(z_i\) winsorized \(\pm\) winsor_z. Weights (weight_mode). "equal": peptides get weight 1. "se_invvar": weights proportional inverse standard error (analogous denominator "asin"). "n_eff_sqrt": $$        w_i = \sqrt{ n_{g1} \hat p_{g1} + n_{g2} \hat p_{g2} },      $$ .e. square root expected number positives across groups. Combine single test statistic (aggregate_stat). Let \(w_i\) weights \(z_i\) peptide-level z-scores. aggregate_stat = "stouffer" strat_bins = 0: $$        T_{\mathrm{obs}} =          \frac{\sum_i w_i z_i}{\sqrt{\sum_i w_i^2}} .      $$ aggregate_stat = "stouffer" strat_bins numeric vector pooled prevalence cutpoints (0 1), peptides binned pooled prevalence $$        \frac{n_{g1}\hat p_{g1} + n_{g2}\hat p_{g2}}{n_{g1} + n_{g2}},      $$ Stouffer statistic \(T_b\) computed within bin. mean bin-level z-scores reported \(T_{\mathrm{obs}}\). example, strat_bins includes 0.10 0.20, peptides pooled prevalence (0.10, 0.20] share bin. Multiplicity. multiple-testing correction performed; p_perm returned computed. Input requirements. exist_col treated 0/1 presence. must one positive per (subject_id, peptide_id, group_col, group_value); paired designs can two positives across two group levels. Violations trigger error. Example (group levels /B): single subject peptide, may =1 B=0 (=0 B=1, =1 B=1), two rows =1 (two rows B=1). Non-peptide ranks specified rank_cols must resolvable peptide library (see peptide_library ). Peptide library resolution. rank_cols includes non-"peptide_id" ranks, peptide library required. resolved following order: explicit peptide_library argument. x$peptide_library x phip_data attached library. get_peptide_library() phiperio (always available dependency).

title: Forest Plot of Top/Bottom Raw Stouffer T by Rank — forestplot
code: # in this example we mock the output of compute_delta with a simple # data.frame - it works the same set.seed(1) n <- 20 results_tbl <- data.frame(   rank = rep("species", n),   feature = paste0("feat_", seq_len(n)),   group1 = "control",   group2 = "treated",   design = "case-control",   T_obs = rnorm(n, sd = 2),   p_perm = runif(n),   T_obs_stand = rnorm(n),   Z_from_p = qnorm(1 - runif(n) / 2) * sign(rnorm(n)) )  out <- forestplot(   results_tbl,   rank_of_interest = "species",   statistic_to_plot = "T",   n_neg_each = 5,   n_pos_each = 5,   left_label = "More in control",   right_label = "More in treated",   use_diverging_colors = TRUE,   font_family = "sans" )  print(out$plot)
